teaching_claim: For z[n]=exp(j pi n/2), either real or imaginary projection vanishes at alternate integer samples while the joint complex magnitude remains one.

thumbnail.result: PASS: the four cardinal orbit positions, counterclockwise arrow, amber round-dot real strip, blue square-dot imaginary strip, and unit-magnitude verdict remain distinguishable in both themes.

numerical_contract.rotation: counterclockwise for positive omega under engineering j

visual_contract.layout: A unit-circle orbit occupies the left side; two aligned right-side stem strips share n=0..3; a compact bottom strip states the invariant magnitude.
visual_contract.discrete_plot: Only integer stems and individual dots are drawn. No segment connects adjacent samples or implies between-sample values.

palette.#e2903a: directly labelled Re / cosine projection, stems, round sample dots, and horizontal cue
palette.#4c8dd6: directly labelled Im / sine projection, stems, square sample dots, and vertical cue
palette.currentColor: orbit, spokes, axes, phase/value labels, direction arrow, and magnitude verdict

visual_contract.non_color_cues: Direct Re/Im labels, upper/lower placement, horizontal/vertical cues, round versus square sample dots, explicit arrays, and numbered orbit positions duplicate every color meaning.

accessibility.labeling: aria-labelledby references a concise title and a factual description containing the orbit order, both projection arrays, and invariant magnitude
accessibility.theme: All neutral text and strokes use currentColor; full-size and 320 px light/dark renders were visually inspected.
accessibility.canonical_phase: The n=2 label explicitly displays phi=+pi, consistent with (-pi,pi].

defects: The counterclockwise direction label intruded into the projection-panel boundary.
iterations.fix: Moved the direction label into the open upper-right quadrant of the unit circle without changing the orbit arrow or any data geometry.

embed_for_closing_owner: <Figure src="./figures/phasor-projections.svg" alt="A unit phasor advances counterclockwise through four quarter-turn positions while separate cosine and sine stem plots show the synchronized samples 1, 0, -1, 0 and 0, 1, 0, -1." caption="The phasor never vanishes: a zero in one projection is carried by its quadrature partner." />
